questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Caltech is one of the best universities in the world. Furthermore, it is one of the best within the fields that I am interestet in (astronomy and chemistry). This also means that the university offers courses that I am unable to take at UCPH sush as comsochemistry. 
In addition to this, Caltech is located in Pasadena near Los Angles which means that there is a lot to do/experience in close proximity to the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I t was pretty easy to find the information that you would need. Also people are were welcomming/open to help if you have any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They did 1,5 weeks of orientation, first international student orientation and then freshmen orientation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They did way too much orientation and a lot of the freshmen orientation stuff is either not relevant or only relevant if you are 17 and moving out for the first time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to stay on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You also have to be a part of their meal plan

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a bit expensive but also pretty nice that you don't have to worry about finding housing while you are there. Also the housing that international/excahnge students stay at (Bechtel) is pretty nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have add/drop day so that you can change courses after trying them out for a week or two which is pretty nice.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a websitepretty much like we do at UCPH where you sign up for courses. They then need to be approved by your study advisor

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can talk to your study advisor or your academic advisor before choosing courses. They also have a webpage with review of the course from previous years-

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. If you take upper level undergrad/grad courses it is usually not a problem to get the courses that you want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make use of the add/drop period

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have some very nice courses that we don't have at home, so take advange of that.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They have a core curriculum that they need to get through in their 1./2. year, so a lot of the courses that we do at home in our major, they don't do until their 3./4. year.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They have more courses in a term (4+) but way less hours pr course pr week. Usually it is 3 hours of lecture and then one office hour. The rest is self sudying

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The elements of quantum chemistry
X-ray crystallography
The formation and evolution of planetary systems 
Research project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The formation and evolution of planetary systems was a great introductory course for planetary science. Even though I am chemist a could easily follow the course and the professor and TA are both amazing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe not so unexpected but we did a lot of trips during the weekends/thanksgiving. These added a bunch of expences

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and accommodation is expensive, but mandatory

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a huge area with different sports facilities that you can use for free. If you want to join clubs you need to be proactive about it, is club fair day isn't until the end of the term right before you leave

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost anything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the great, free sports facilities

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of great national and state parks within driving distance of Pasadena, such as Joshua Tree and Sequoia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to adjust. It is not that different from Denmark, and they also have a lot of international students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The incomming freshmen are pretty young so maybe just focus on getting to know the juniors/seniors

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not a lot of huge cultural differences just smaller ones

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very welcoming/talkative so it is pretty easy to get to know people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You are there for a really short time, so make sure you get the most out of it.
Even though it is a really good school, remember that you are also there to enjoy some time away from UCPH and get some new experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The academic level might in some cases be higher than at UCPH so be smrt about the number/courses that you take

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the amazing experiences also away from campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out/prioritizing what we wanted to do on the weekends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
